name: Metropolis (1927)
summary: A city of towers, sky bridges and hidden machines, from the 1927 silent film.
description: From the Sci-Fi 360 journey: Metropolis' avenues, statues of labor, flyers and the central tower.
learningObjectives: Discuss how technology can divide or connect a society.

display.title: METROPOLIS
display.author: FRITZ LANG · THEA VON HARBOU
display.themeLine: A gleaming city built on hidden labor asks who its machines really serve.

hotspots.label: Sky traffic
hotspots.title: Flying cars and sky bridges
hotspots.text: Metropolis imagined a city of towers linked by sky bridges, with flying traffic and airships, a picture of the future that still shapes science fiction.

facts.text: Fritz Lang's silent film premiered in Berlin on 10 January 1927.

hotspots.label: The machine
hotspots.title: Who runs the machines?
hotspots.text: The rich live in towers above while workers run the machines below. The film asks who the city's machines really serve.
hotspots.archive: Down there, the workers who keep it running.

hotspots.label: Head, hands, heart
hotspots.title: Head, hands and heart
hotspots.text: The film's closing message: the mediator between head and hands must be the heart.

facts.text: Lost footage was rediscovered in Buenos Aires in 2008.

hotspots.archive: The head and the hands need a heart.

facts.text: Fritz Lang's silent film premiered in Berlin on 10 January 1927.
Thea von Harbou wrote the screenplay and the novel it came from.
The rich live in towers above while workers run the machines below.
Its closing message: the mediator between head and hands must be the heart.
Lost footage was rediscovered in Buenos Aires in 2008.
